factChecks.note: Left-to-right order is EFFORT (hand) -> LOAD (grey block) -> FULCRUM (triangle) -- load is correctly between effort and fulcrum. The physical geometry itself is correct.

styleComplianceNotes: White/near-white background, single lever arrangement rendered correctly.
physicalImplausibilityNotes: Label duplication defect: both EFFORT and FULCRUM are labelled TWICE. The duplicate EFFORT labels are both near the correct location (harmless redundancy). The duplicate FULCRUM label is a genuine problem: one instance is correctly positioned next to the actual triangular fulcrum at the right end, but the other floats near the LOAD block in the middle of the image -- exactly where a learner could mistake it for marking the fulcrum's position. This is a real, confirmable label-placement defect, not a geometry error.
overallFindings: RETRY. Underlying physical geometry (fulcrum/effort/load ordering) is correct, but a duplicated and misplaced FULCRUM label risks teaching the wrong fulcrum position. Requires one correction attempt with an explicit instruction against duplicate/floating labels.
